quote: So it's still empty lot, but I know the home is built. It's a single family. Right?
stewart_read: The rep's mapping system shows an empty lot at the address, but rather than treating this as a blocker or hiding the discrepancy, the rep names it plainly and confirms directly with the customer. This is the admit-and-recover pattern, not a dodge or fabrication.
coaching_implication: Positive example worth reinforcing — the rep didn't let a system limitation stall the call or create doubt; replay as a model of transparent recovery.

stewart_read: The customer names his son as a co-owner on the title, which triggers the same protocol as spouse-on-title: the co-decision-maker should be folded into the appointment. The rep says 'Okay' and moves straight to utility company without ever raising whether the son should be on the Monday call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep simply logged the fact and moved to the next verify item without registering its protocol significance. Strategic read would require the rep circling back later to include the son, which never happens — so reactive is the supported read.
coaching_implication: Flag directly: when a co-owner is named, the rep should ask 'will he be able to join the call too?' at booking. This appointment goes out with a title-holder unaccounted for, which is a structural vulnerability the closer should know about.

quote: Still we are waiting for our one bill. We have not received anything yet.
stewart_read: No bill amount exists because the household just moved in and hasn't received a first bill yet — this is a genuine no_bill_captured scenario, not a rep miss. The rep's only real option here was to ask for the prior residence's bill or Portland General average, which wasn't attempted.
coaching_implication: Not a rep failure to flip a number that didn't exist, but a missed chance to ask 'what were you paying at your last place?' as a proxy anchor — worth naming as a technique for new-mover leads.

quote: We will decide, that how much is there because we'll have to evaluate how much you are going to charge me monthly and how much I'm getting the the bill of, Fortnite.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep his own framing for why he'd move forward — comparing Ion's monthly charge against his utility bill once it arrives. This is a customer-volunteered curiosity hook the rep could reflect back ('exactly what the specialist will lay out side by side for you') but instead the rep just confirms the day.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may have judged the point self-evident and not worth restating. But nothing in the transcript shows the rep verbally anchoring to this framing, so the miss stands.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to mirror customer-stated evaluation criteria back before booking — it reinforces why the appointment matters to the customer specifically.

quote: Portland Journal. Okay. And I need that. Yep. How much do you spend on a monthly average?
stewart_read: Rep does ask for the average bill directly per script, immediately after capturing the utility company — correct sequencing even though the answer turned out to be unavailable.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed on the ask itself; the gap is entirely on follow-up given the 'no bill yet' answer (see the prior cherry-pick on proxy anchoring).

quote: Have a great day. I'll text you to remind you.
stewart_read: The rep locks day and time but never runs the full button-up: no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake before signing off with a text-reminder promise only.
coaching_implication: Coach the full button-up sequence — the appointment is booked but fragile on show-rate mechanics; a specific block-time and computer-readiness instruction should be added before ending calls like this.
